descriptors.R: nominee of the party that won both houses of Congress in 1946 and has been out of the presidency since 1933
descriptors.D: nominee of the party in office since 1933, nominating the sitting President, who succeeded to the office in 1945
descriptors.O: nominee of a states'-rights movement of Southern members of the administration party who broke with it over its civil-rights program; on the ballot mainly in the South

compile_desc.R: the party that has held a majority in Congress since the 1946 elections

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including the new Progressive party's nominee, a former Vice President who broke with the administration over relations with the Soviet Union, and a Socialist nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Dewey, Truman, Thurmond, Wallace, Warren, Barkley, Fielding Wright, Glen Taylor, Norman Thomas or Franklin Roosevelt

slice_sources.men: 1940 and 1950 censuses interpolated to November 1948; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only; American Indians in Arizona and New Mexico won the vote by court rulings that summer; Black voters here vote heavily Democratic since 1936; calibrated to certified 1948 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1948, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1948 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1948, white adults in the eleven former Confederate states, 18+ in Georgia (voting age 18 since 1943; poll tax repealed 1945); calibrated to certified 1948 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1948, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states (18+ in Georgia); registration has risen since the white primary fell in 1944, but poll taxes, literacy tests and intimidation keep most disfranchised, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1940–1950 interpolation to November 1948, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; no state let aliens vote.

masks: the President's policy of aid to Greece and Turkey
the nominee of the party out of power
